Amazon to invest €16 billion in Germany in 2027 
Company News
Amazon announces plan to invest €16 billion in Germany in 2027
Since 2010, Amazon has invested over €100 billion in Germany, underscoring the country as one of the most important to Amazon worldwide. 
Share
Written by 
Amazon Staff
6 min read
Key takeaways
Amazon will invest €16 billion in Germany in 2027, supporting data center and AI infrastructure.
The investment will also support satellite connectivity through Amazon Leo, logistics expansion, and new Prime Video content.
Amazon is also committing to more sustainable infrastructure and water stewardship across Germany.
Amazon plans to invest more than €16 billion ($18 billion) in 
Germany
 in 2027. The new investments span jobs
,
 technology, and infrastructure. These include the expansion of data centers and AI infrastructure, high-speed satellite internet through 
Amazon Leo
, new logistics projects across the country, and a major new production slate by 
Prime Video
.
The company announced the investment on October 20 at the Invest in Germany Summit, held by the Federal Government in Berlin. The new investments build on another recently announced milestone: since 2010, Amazon has invested over €100 billion in Germany, underscoring the country as one of the most important to Amazon worldwide.
Friedrich Merz (German chancellor), David Zapolsky (chief global affairs and legal officer at Amazon), and Katherina Reiche (federal minister for economic affairs and energy).
"Germany is a hub of innovation and one of the most attractive investment opportunities in Europe. That is why we have invested more than €100 billion here since 2010, and why we plan to invest an additional €16 billion in 2027. We want German businesses, communities, and creators to have the infrastructure and tools they need to compete and grow," said David Zapolsky, Amazon’s chief global affairs and legal officer, with the German chancellor Friedrich Merz at the Invest in Germany Summit.
Katherina Reiche, federal minister for economic affairs and energy, said:

"Amazon's investment is a clear vote of confidence in Germany as a location for the future. High-performance data centers are the foundation of the digital economy. With the data wealth of our industry, we also have the potential to become a global leader in industrial AI. These are exactly the kinds of investments we need: they strengthen Germany's position in international technology competition and create value and jobs in the process."
Amazon unveils next-gen Proteus robot as part of €10 billion European investment in its fulfillment network
The new Proteus and additional robotics expansions in Europe are designed to support employees by taking on physically strenuous tasks.
Amazon is currently opening a second research lab for 
robotics
 and artificial intelligence in Berlin, doubling its research presence in the capital. Amazon’s research will further develop intelligent collaboration between people and technology so that customers receive their orders even faster and more reliably and employees are supported in the best possible way. The new lab creates highly specialized roles, including applied scientists, robotics hardware engineers, robotics software engineers, and robotics systems engineers.
Rocco Bräuniger, Amazon Germany country manager, added: "We have already created over 40,000 permanent jobs, built more than 100 sites, and invested more than €100 billion in Germany—and we are far from done. Customers expect us to keep innovating, and that is exactly what we will do: with faster logistics, cutting-edge AI, high-speed satellite internet, and German stories that captivate Prime Video audiences around the world."
Investing  €4.8 billion to expand AWS cloud and AI infrastructure in Germany
Germany is among the most innovative countries on the globe, and with its cloud business, Amazon has long been supporting German companies with the technology to innovate and compete. As part of the €16 billion euros investment, the company plans to invest €4.8 billion in 2027 to expand its AWS Europe (Frankfurt) Region, continuing to meet customer demand for advanced cloud and AI services.
Amazon has created more than 40,000 permanent jobs in Germany, among them are 3,000 AWS employees. The company has also invested double-digit billions of euros in its cloud infrastructure since launching the AWS Europe (Frankfurt) Region in October 2014 and the 
AWS European Sovereign Cloud
 in Germany, which has been generally available since January 2026.
"In a fast-moving world, companies need infrastructure they can rely on—secure, available, and built to help them stay ahead. They need the broadest choice of services to meet their individual needs," said Stefan Höchbauer, vice president of AWS global sales for Germany and Europe Central. "That is exactly what AWS offers. We will keep investing so that German innovation keeps thriving. As part of the investments, €4.8 billion is planned to expand the AWS Europe (Frankfurt) Region through 2027."
Millions of students can now get access to a free year of Kiro from AWS
AWS is giving students at 132 universities across 18 countries a full year of free access to Kiro, so they enter the workforce ready to build with AI from day one.
Since 2023, Amazon and Siemens have been offering apprenticeships certified by the German chamber of commerce and industry (IHK) for IT and electronics technicians at Amazon data centers in Hesse and Brandenburg.
Amazon and IHK launched Germany's first national cloud certification, the Cloud Business Expert (IHK), driving digital skills development across the country through the AWS Tech Alliance and a wide range of training programs. The Alliance has reached more than 20,000 students in Germany since launching in December 2023.
This year, Amazon also announced Kiro for students, giving millions of students at 132 universities across 18 countries—including Germany—a full year of 
free access to Kiro
, a professional, agentic AI development environment, so they enter the workforce ready to build with AI from day one.
Investing in Amazon Leo and collaborating with the European space industry
Amazon Leo
 is a satellite network in low Earth orbit designed to provide fast, reliable internet to households, schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies in areas that existing networks don’t reach—including across Germany. Amazon Leo has secured 24 launches with the 
European launch provider Arianespace
.
The economic research institute Oxford Economics projects that Amazon Leo’s second-largest economic impact in Europe will be felt in Germany—home to several ArianeGroup sites as well as MT Aerospace, one of ArianeGroup's most important suppliers.
Everything you need to know about Amazon Leo, Amazon’s satellite broadband network
Get answers to your questions about how Amazon will provide internet connectivity from space.
Expanding  Amazon’s  logistics footprint across Germany
Amazon is expanding its logistics footprint in Germany, investing in modern technologies across its locations, including robotics that drive ergonomic working conditions for employees and even faster, more reliable service for customers.
The comprehensive modernization of existing fulfillment centers in Bad Hersfeld, Dortmund, and Werne will be completed in 2027, while modernization work in Koblenz, Pforzheim, and Rheinberg will continue through 2028. This year, Amazon is opening a fulfillment center in Zweibrücken—which is already creating jobs—and a new fulfillment center is being built in Könnern. These already-announced logistics projects account for more than 3,000 new jobs in Germany.
Amazon offers access to logistics careers regardless of prior qualifications, with full-time employees reaching an average annual gross salary of €41,600 after two years in addition to benefits, including up to €4,500 for professional development.
New Prime Video productions in Germany
Beyond infrastructure investments, Amazon is also strengthening Germany as a creative hub. Amazon has produced more than 65 local titles in Germany, working with leading German production companies including UFA, Constantin Film, and Bavaria Film across filming locations from Berlin to Munich.
Prime Video
 has announced new movies including 
Der erste letzte Tag
 (The First Last Day), based on a novel by Sebastian Fitzek; 
and Drive – The Pretenders
 starring Lisa-Marie Koroll and Amin Bahmeed; and 
Holey Moley – Minigolf Extreme,
 hosted by Johannes B. Kerner, Ralf Schmitz, and field reporter SelfieSandra. These are just some of the more than 15 productions coming to Germany through the end of 2027.
Prime Video to invest $2 billion in Latin America between 2027 and 2030
The investment spans original programming and live sports across the region—with more than 25 new titles coming in 2027 alone.
This commitment to local storytelling is reflected on screen, with European works accounting for more than a third of everything customers see on the Prime Video homepage in Germany.
Investing in sustainability and communities across Germany
As Germany’s largest corporate 
purchaser of carbon-free energy
, Amazon has enabled carbon-free energy projects across Germany with a combined capacity of more than 1.3 GW, including 
wind farm projects in the North and Baltic Seas
. Once fully operational, these projects are expected to generate enough electricity to power the equivalent of more than 1.8 million German households annually.
Sustainability is equally central to Amazon's data center operations. The company is building the world's most sustainable cloud infrastructure—combining industry-leading energy and water efficiency, circular economy practices, and AI-powered innovation—to help customers decarbonize while advancing Amazon's 
Climate Pledge
 goal to achieve net-zero carbon by 2040.
Roughly 95 percent of the time, Amazon's data centers in Germany use free air cooling with no water involved. When evaporative cooling is needed on the warmest days, all planned data centers in Germany will use harvested rainwater to minimize demands on community water resources and reduce potential stormwater runoff.
Amazon's water conservation and replenishment efforts around the world
Get the latest updates on how we’re reducing our water footprint and investing in innovations to address water scarcity.
Amazon is committed to being water positive by 2030—returning more water to communities than it uses across its data center operations—and is already 75 percent of the way there. As part of this commitment, the company is supporting two water projects in Frankfurt and recently announced 
a third water replenishment project with NABU
 (Nature and Biodiversity Conservation Union) expected to return more than 750 million liters of water to the groundwater supply annually.
In its data center locations, Amazon's community engagement program, InCommunities, drives local impact across four pillars: STEM education, local skills development, sustainability, and hyperlocal social impact. Key initiatives include coding workshops with 
TecHeroes
, the first German 
Think Big Space
 in Kelsterbach, a Girls' Tech Day, and a pioneering 
EnergyCloud
 project converting surplus renewable energy into free heating for families in the Frankfurt Region.
Amazon's Berlin headquarters hosts KiezLab, which has provided 1,400 square meters of free community space since it opened and brings 125 nonprofit organizations free educational programs and workshops. The Goods for Good program has also allowed social organizations to order free products, with more than 200 partners expected by the end of 2026.
Amazon’s European 
Disaster Relief Hub
 in Leipzig enables the company to deliver free relief supplies across Europe within 72 hours—most recently providing support for the 
French wildfires
 in the summer of 2026.
